claim: WOMAD Cáceres 2026 is its 33rd edition, held 7-10 May, free entry, staged across Plaza Mayor, Plaza de San Jorge, Plaza de Santa María and palaces in the historic centre.
quote: WOMAD Cáceres 2026 will celebrate its 33rd edition from May 7-10. The festival features 21 groups from 14 countries... The event is completely free.

claim: Direct Renfe train Madrid (Atocha) to Cáceres takes about 3h, departing roughly every four hours; bus from Estación Sur takes about 4h, with train the best price/speed balance.
quote: There is a direct train departing from Madrid-Puerta de Atocha... services departing every four hours... taking approximately 3h 7m... The best way to travel from Madrid to Cáceres is by taking a train.

claim: San Jorge 2026 peaks 22 April: a 7pm parade of 3,100+ people and 27 dragons (incl. a 14m giant), then at 10pm in Plaza Mayor the Atakama company stages The Legend of St George, ending with the dragon slain, fireworks and a golden-hen hunt.
quote: At 10:00 PM in Plaza Mayor, the Atakama theatre company presents The Legend of St George. After the performance, once St George has slain the dragon, there will be fireworks and a hunt for golden hens begins.

claim: The San Jorge dragon-and-entourage parade is scheduled Tuesday 22 April 2026 from 8pm, finishing in Plaza Mayor via Gran Vía.
quote: The dragon and entourage parade will take place on Tuesday, April 22, 2026, beginning at 8:00 PM... concluding at Plaza Mayor.

claim: Cáceres summers (June to mid-September) are very hot and dry, with July-August highs around 34°C and peaks of 39-40°C; the best windows are April-May and mid-September to mid-October.
quote: Summer in Cáceres runs from June to mid-September and is very hot and sunny... Highs are usually about 34 °C... the temperature normally reaches 39/40 °C... The best times to visit Cáceres are the months of April and May and from mid-September to mid-October.

claim: From Seville, the direct bus (Plaza de Armas, 5 daily) is the best option at about 3h15 for €19-45, driving is fastest at 2h39 (261km), and the train via Renfe takes about 4h47.
quote: Bus — 3h 15m with €19–45 cost. This is marked as the best option and offers direct service departing five times daily from Sevilla's Plaza de Armas station... Drive Duration: 2 hours 39 minutes Distance: 261 km.

claim: Cáceres to Lisbon is reachable by bus (cheapest, ~€12, ~3h55), train (~4h43, ~€58) or flight via Badajoz Airport, the nearest airport to Cáceres.
quote: The cheapest way to travel from Cáceres to Lisbon is a bus with an average price of $15 (€12)... The nearest airport to Cáceres appears to be Badajoz Airport, which serves flights to major destinations like Lisbon.

claim: Travellers say one day is enough to walk the walled old town (3-4 hours plus an evening paseo), but two days lets you explore museums and surroundings without rushing.
quote: If you don't have very much time, one day is enough to see pretty much everything. Walking the area inside the walls, museums and walls takes about 3-4 hours... two days is ideal if you want to explore the city more thoroughly without feeling rushed.

claim: The compact walled old town is explored on foot; landmark towers and the cathedral charge small fees (Bujaco Tower and Concatedral de Santa María tower roughly €2.50 each), while the squares, Arco de la Estrella and Jewish quarter are free to wander.
quote: Bujaco Tower (Museum): Entry cost is €2.50... Concatedral de Santa María Tower: Entry cost is €2.50.
